description: RAGAS SingleTurnSample fixtures: user_input, response, retrieved_contexts, reference. Contexts are paragraphs from corpus.json; responses are grounded in those contexts.

samples.user_input: How does contextual retrieval fix the lost-context problem in chunked documents?
retrieved_contexts: The main failure mode that contextual retrieval fixes is the loss of context that happens when a document is split into chunks. A chunk that says 'revenue grew 3% over the previous quarter' does not mention the company or the quarter, so neither a dense embedding nor a BM25 index can match it to a question that names them. With the situating context added, the chunk becomes self-describing.

Contextual retrieval is an indexing technique in which every chunk of a document is prepended with a short, chunk-specific context before it is embedded. The context is written by a language model that reads the whole document together with the chunk, and it states what the chunk is about and how it relates to the rest of the document.
samples.response: Contextual retrieval prepends each chunk with a short context generated by a language model that has read the whole document. A chunk such as 'revenue grew 3% over the previous quarter' does not name the company or quarter on its own, so embeddings and BM25 cannot match it to a question that does; adding the situating context makes the chunk self-describing.
samples.reference: It prepends every chunk with a chunk-specific context written by an LLM that reads the entire document, so chunks that lost their surrounding context (like a revenue figure with no company or quarter) become self-describing and can be matched by dense embeddings and BM25.

samples.user_input: What is the minimum prompt length that Claude Haiku 4.5 will cache?
retrieved_contexts: The minimum cacheable prefix length depends on the model. Claude Haiku 3.5 required 2048 tokens; Claude Haiku 4.5 requires 4096 tokens; Claude Opus 5 caches prefixes as short as 512 tokens. Prefixes shorter than the minimum are silently not cached: the request succeeds, but usage reports zero cache creation and zero cache read tokens.
samples.response: Claude Haiku 4.5 requires a prefix of at least 4096 tokens before it will cache it. Shorter prefixes are silently not cached: the request succeeds but reports zero cache creation and zero cache read tokens.
samples.reference: 4096 tokens; shorter prefixes are silently not cached.

samples.user_input: How many cache breakpoints can a single request have and what is their TTL?
retrieved_contexts: Each request may contain at most four cache breakpoints, set with a cache_control block of type ephemeral. The default time to live is five minutes and a cache read refreshes the timer at no extra cost, so a stream of requests that share a prefix and start less than five minutes apart keeps the entry warm indefinitely.
samples.response: A request can carry at most four cache breakpoints, each declared with a cache_control block of type ephemeral. The default TTL is five minutes, and every cache read refreshes the timer for free, so requests sharing a prefix that arrive less than five minutes apart keep the entry warm.
samples.reference: At most four breakpoints per request; the ephemeral cache has a default five-minute TTL that each cache read refreshes.

samples.user_input: How does reciprocal rank fusion combine dense and sparse results in Qdrant?
retrieved_contexts: Qdrant's Universal Query API executes the whole hybrid pipeline in one request. Two prefetch branches retrieve the top candidates from the dense and sparse indexes, and a fusion query of type RRF merges the two ranked lists with reciprocal rank fusion, which scores each document by the sum of 1 divided by (k plus its rank) across the lists.

Hybrid search combines a dense vector index with a sparse lexical index. The dense vectors, here 384-dimensional embeddings from BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 compared with cosine distance, capture semantic similarity. The sparse vectors are BM25 term weights produced client-side by FastEmbed; the collection declares the IDF modifier so that Qdrant applies inverse document frequency on the server.
samples.response: Two prefetch branches fetch the top candidates from the dense and the sparse (BM25) indexes, and an RRF fusion query merges the two ranked lists. Reciprocal rank fusion scores each document by summing 1 / (k + rank) over the lists in which it appears, all within a single Universal Query API request.
samples.reference: Dense and sparse prefetch branches each return a ranked list, and an RRF fusion query scores each document as the sum over lists of 1/(k + rank), producing one merged ranking in a single query request.

samples.user_input: Why is HNSW disabled for the ColBERT vectors?
retrieved_contexts: The fused list can itself be reranked by a ColBERT multivector. ColBERT encodes every token as a 128-dimensional vector and scores a document with MaxSim: for each query token it takes the maximum similarity over the document tokens and sums those maxima. Because ColBERT is only used to rerank a few dozen prefetched candidates, its HNSW index is disabled by setting m to zero, which avoids indexing millions of token vectors.
samples.response: Because ColBERT only reranks a few dozen prefetched candidates with MaxSim, it never needs an approximate nearest-neighbour search over the whole collection. Setting HNSW m to zero disables the index and avoids the cost of indexing millions of 128-dimensional token vectors.
samples.reference: ColBERT is used only to rerank a small set of prefetched candidates, so an HNSW index over its token vectors would be pure overhead; m=0 disables it.

samples.user_input: What retry policy does the Cohere rerank client use for 429 errors?
retrieved_contexts: The rerank client uses a full-jitter retry policy for rate limits: at most five retries, with a delay drawn uniformly between zero and the minimum of thirty seconds and one second times two to the power of the attempt number. A Retry-After header from the API is honoured when it is longer than the jittered delay.
samples.response: It retries up to five times with full jitter: each delay is drawn uniformly between zero and min(30 seconds, 1 second × 2^attempt). If the API sends a Retry-After header that is longer than the jittered delay, the header value is used instead.
samples.reference: Full-jitter exponential backoff with max_retries=5, base_delay=1s and max_delay=30s (delay uniform in [0, min(30, 2^attempt)]), honouring Retry-After when it is larger.

samples.user_input: Which fields does a rag.dlq entry contain?
retrieved_contexts: Every failed pipeline stage writes an entry to a Redis Stream named rag.dlq. Each entry carries exactly five fields: document_id, stage, error_type, error_message and timestamp. The stage is one of extraction, chunking, indexing, retrieval, rerank or orchestration, and the timestamp is an ISO 8601 UTC value with millisecond precision.
samples.response: A rag.dlq entry has exactly five fields: document_id, stage, error_type, error_message and timestamp. The timestamp is an ISO 8601 UTC value with millisecond precision.
samples.reference: document_id, stage, error_type, error_message and timestamp.

samples.user_input: Which environment variables must be identical on n8n main and worker instances?
retrieved_contexts: Three settings are mandatory on every instance: EXECUTIONS_MODE must be queue, QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_HOST must point at the shared Redis, and N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY must be identical everywhere so that workers can decrypt credentials stored by the main instance. WEBHOOK_URL must also be set on the main instance and on the workers, otherwise nodes running on a worker build webhook URLs that resolve to localhost:5678.
samples.response: EXECUTIONS_MODE=queue, QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_HOST pointing at the shared Redis, and N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY must match on every instance so workers can decrypt credentials; WEBHOOK_URL must also be set on both main and workers so webhook URLs do not resolve to localhost:5678.
samples.reference: EXECUTIONS_MODE (queue), QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_HOST, N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY and WEBHOOK_URL must be set consistently on main and worker instances.

samples.user_input: What happens if WEBHOOK_URL is not set on n8n workers?
retrieved_contexts: Three settings are mandatory on every instance: EXECUTIONS_MODE must be queue, QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_HOST must point at the shared Redis, and N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY must be identical everywhere so that workers can decrypt credentials stored by the main instance. WEBHOOK_URL must also be set on the main instance and on the workers, otherwise nodes running on a worker build webhook URLs that resolve to localhost:5678.

In queue mode n8n is split into a main instance, worker instances and webhook processors. The main instance owns the editor, timers and trigger registration; it pushes execution ids onto a Bull queue in Redis and workers pick them up, load the workflow from PostgreSQL and run it.
samples.response: Nodes that execute on a worker build their webhook URLs from the worker's own defaults, so the URLs resolve to localhost:5678 instead of the public address. Setting WEBHOOK_URL on the workers as well as on the main instance prevents this.
samples.reference: Workers generate webhook URLs that point at localhost:5678, so callbacks fail; WEBHOOK_URL must be set on workers as well as main.

samples.user_input: How are documents formatted before being sent to the reranker?
retrieved_contexts: Cohere's v2 rerank API takes the documents as plain strings. Semi-structured chunks are rendered as YAML with the keys in a fixed order, title then context then text, because the order in which the reranker reads the fields affects its scores. The response contains an index for each result that points back into the list of documents that was sent, plus a relevance score between zero and one; the service maps the indexes back to the original chunks and sorts by relevance score.
samples.response: Each chunk is rendered as a YAML string with its keys in a fixed order — title, then context, then text — because Cohere's v2 rerank endpoint accepts plain strings and the field order influences the scores. The returned indexes are mapped back to the original chunks and sorted by relevance score.
samples.reference: Chunks are serialised to YAML strings with a fixed key order (title, context, text) since the v2 rerank API only accepts strings; results are mapped back via their index and sorted by relevance_score.
